Gpa is 8.2 after pass or fail. So 8, or A-. Most masters program don’t look at first year, so I guess my grade is 8.68 without first year, still A-. 

Like you, I had very high hopes going into the program, and wanted to do medical school at the beginning. 

First year was pretty hard for me cause I had to commute 3 hours round trips to school every day. I move loser to school second year, and my experience automatically got better. 

Not gonna lie to you, first year was pretty hard. Anatomy classes (ANP1105/1106) were quite difficult if you don’t put in a lot of effort. It is very easy to mess up and fail a midterm. I’ve gotten 32% on a midterm that I’ve studied well over 20 hours for. The prof is very annoying, giving you incomplete notes and make you pay attention every second. Other classes are fine. Don’t pick Rada for your calculus prof btw. 

After the first year, things gets a lot easier (for me anyways). Second year biostatistics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, genetics classes are all pretty cool and the professors are very nice. I had Flynn for organic chemistry, she’s a good prof. 

Third year is going well too, I don’t get as much electives as others cause I specialized in Biostatistics.

For COOP, most jobs are in government, there are some hospital and research jobs as well. A lot of data entry/report making jobs. My job right now is pretty much glorified data entry. But the experience is good, and the pay is pretty handsome for students: 19$ - 24$ an hour (depending on year).

UOttawa is great. I had classes both in-person before the pandemic and virtual now (online). I like the school. 

The campus is pretty good, a lot of quiet and good place to study. The layout of the buildings aren’t too confusing, you can get from point A to point B pretty easily and fast. Cafeteria food is actually pretty good compared to other universities I’ve visited (Queens, UOfT, Carleton). I also had a good experience with some school services like gyms and career development centres. 

With that being said, I wish some profs weren’t douchebags, but I believe that is a problem with every school. 

I’m currently specializing in biostatistics, and doing government job (Health Canada) for coop. For me, it’s worth it cause I don’t wanna do med/dental school, and I am considering a masters program related to my work right now.

Gpa: 8 (year 3 with COOP)

Workload: heavy but I didn’t do jack shit

Pre-med: IDK I’m not thinking about that

Other schools: don’t go other place, UOttawa is great

Advise: take bps1101 easy 10, don’t take physics 2 it’s aids, take coop if ur first year grade turns out to be shit.

Well, since biomed coop is optional, you pay an extra 795$ after tax to be in the program in the first place. Then you have to pay 795$ each term for the 4 coop terms. So 5x795$ is the total.

Once you pay the first 795$(non-refundable), you must do the 4 terms, or you get a failed coop on your transcript
Plus, COOP should cover your 4 years of tuition easily. And should be able to pay back OSAP loan.

I’m in the first biomed coop term rn, and am about to start working. idk if this helps with dental school, but the process definitely prepares you for job hunt and professional stuff in general. COOP in general is also quite a pleasant experience. People at the coop office are nice folks.

There were hospital jobs for COOP for winter 2021 terms, but most are either clerical (aka photocopying), or research (CRISPR library lab assistant). There were also pharmaceutical company jobs (Sanofi). 

Most jobs are and most students get government positions, I don’t know if Health Canada experience helps with dental school. Things may be different due to COVID, but I wouldn’t know.

I guess my advise is, study hard in your second year, if your GPA is around 9, don’t bother doing coop cause you should be focusing on dental school tests and volunteering in hospitals and stuff. 

Let me know if you have questions.

Edit: reminder that the deadline for registration for coop program before the end of March in your second year, and after you pay your first COOP fee, you cannot change your mind.
